tested_scope: One bounded non-destructive model using only current connected Chat GitHub mutation/read selector schemas plus own Part124 checkpoint. Compared repository_id-addressed mutation availability, owner/name content CAS plus an own-state pinned repository_id sentinel, and any discoverable connector-side pinned repository/install binding. The race tested was PRECHECK -> same-name target rebind -> WRITE; no repository delete/recreate/transfer/regrant was executed.

current_contract_observations.scope_note: This is a current connector-schema discovery result, not a claim about all GitHub APIs or future connector actions.

steps: PRECHECK: read current repository identity and confirm owner/name resolves to R1 and repository_id equals the own-state sentinel.
TARGET_REBIND: after precheck and before write, owner/name is rebound to a different repository incarnation R2.
PATH_EQUIVALENCE_CONTROL: R2 may contain the same path P with identical prior content, so the path blob SHA can also equal S; for create-only writes, R2 may instead omit P.
WRITE: invoke the current owner/name-addressed mutation. No observed mutation contract atomically requires repository_id=R1-id or installation/grant identity.

mechanism_results.reason: repository_id is exposed on several read/search selectors but no discovered write contract accepts repository_id as the repository selector or expected-incarnation precondition.

The sentinel can detect a rebind only before the write. A rebind after PRECHECK is not atomically fenced. update_file/delete_file SHA CAS checks path content inside whichever repository owner/name resolves to; an R2 path with identical prior content can present the same content-addressed blob SHA S. create_file has no prior-content SHA and can succeed in R2 when P is absent. Therefore content CAS plus preflight repository_id is not a repository-incarnation CAS.

No current mutation schema discovered in this bounded contract scan exposes expected_repository_id, expected_installation_id, expected_grant_id/epoch, or an equivalent pinned target binding checked atomically with the mutation.

new_narrowing: Part124 established a PRECHECK->WRITE TOCTOU gap. Part125 adds a concrete counterexample showing that path content SHA CAS does not necessarily incidentally close that gap: same-name R2 can recreate the same path with identical prior content and therefore the same Git blob SHA, after which an owner/name update/delete can satisfy the content CAS in the wrong repository incarnation. Unique-path create is even less identity-selective when the path is absent in R2. The remaining blocker is specifically an atomic write-time target-incarnation predicate, not merely observability or path-content CAS.

acceptance.minimal_unresolved_child: A Chat-native mutation contract that atomically binds the effect to the intended repository incarnation (repository_id or equivalent), and when authorization continuity matters to the intended installation/grant epoch, without protected/manual setup, external monotonic coordination, finite monthly/trial/paid quota, or incremental cost.
acceptance.scope_guard: Falsification applies to the current connected Chat GitHub contracts and the modeled same-name rebind with path-equivalence control. It does not assert destructive rebind is likely, does not claim GitHub service-wide impossibility, and does not cover future connector capabilities.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.richer_mode_protected_manual_execution_d: unresolved_for_acceptance: atomic write-time repository/install incarnation binding remains unavailable in the tested connector mutation contracts

conflict_and_idempotency_assessment.content_sha_CAS: still useful for stale path-content conflict inside the repository incarnation selected at write time, but not a repository-incarnation fence
conflict_and_idempotency_assessment.own_state_repository_id_sentinel: useful preflight detector only; not atomic with owner/name write
conflict_and_idempotency_assessment.unique_path_create: useful for duplicate receipt/effect detection only after assuming stable destination identity; not an identity fence
conflict_and_idempotency_assessment.rate_limit_interruption: no same-run retry; interrupted attempt fails closed and continuation is persisted

continuation: Part126: switch to a different CLEAN-safe coordination leaf rather than repeat repository-identity observability. Execute one bounded immutable-claim/no-lease model using unique-path create as the claim transition under a fixed destination-incarnation assumption. Test two concurrent claimers, response loss after successful create, duplicate delivery, abandoned claimant, and takeover without wall-clock leases. Compare permanent monotonic claim, explicit generation-fenced handoff, and lease/timeout takeover. Preserve the repository-incarnation requirement as an orthogonal unresolved child; reject any candidate that needs external hosted coordination, protected/manual arbitration, finite monthly/trial/paid quota, or incremental cost.
